s1.syndrome_frame: Acute neurological deficit with speech disturbance and hemiparesis
key_facts: Noncontrast head CT showed early ischemic changes
CT angiography revealed acute occlusion of the left middle cerebral artery
Chronic occlusion of the left internal carotid artery

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute neurological deficit with speech disturbance and hemiparesis
key_facts: Noncontrast head CT showed early ischemic changes
CT angiography revealed acute occlusion of the left middle cerebral artery
Chronic occlusion of the left internal carotid artery

differentials: Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy, lactic acidosis, and stroke-like episodes
per_call: Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy, lactic acidosis, and stroke-like episodes

shortlist.label: Ischemic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with acute speech disturbance, right-sided weakness, and NIH Stroke Scale score of 19, with noncontrast head CT showing early ischemic changes and CT angiography revealing acute occlusion of the left middle cerebral artery

shortlist.label: Stroke due to atrial fibrillation
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has persistent atrial fibrillation, which is a known risk factor for cardioembolic stroke, and CT angiography revealed acute occlusion of the left middle cerebral artery

shortlist.label: Cardioembolic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has atrial fibrillation and elevated C-reactive protein, with evidence of acute occlusion of the left middle cerebral artery, suggesting a possible cardioembolic source

shortlist.label: Cerebral vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has elevated C-reactive protein and mild pleocytosis in cerebrospinal fluid, which could indicate an inflammatory process such as cerebral vasculitis

shortlist.label: Central nervous system vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has elevated protein in cerebrospinal fluid and evidence of acute occlusion of the left middle cerebral artery, which could be consistent with central nervous system vasculitis

raw.rationale: The patient's persistent atrial fibrillation, acute speech disturbance, right-sided weakness, and imaging findings of early ischemic changes and acute occlusion of the left middle cerebral artery are consistent with a cardioembolic stroke, which is a type of ischemic stroke caused by an embolus originating from the heart.

rejected.label: Ischemic stroke
rejected.why: Too broad, as cardioembolic stroke is a specific subtype of ischemic stroke

rejected.label: Stroke due to atrial fibrillation
rejected.why: Essentially synonymous with cardioembolic stroke in this context, but less specific

rejected.label: Cerebral vasculitis
rejected.why: Not supported by the presence of atrial fibrillation and the pattern of ischemic changes, and would likely have more prominent inflammatory markers

rejected.label: Central nervous system vasculitis
rejected.why: Similar to cerebral vasculitis, not supported by the clinical and imaging findings, and would likely have more systemic symptoms and laboratory evidence of inflammation
